source_caption:
To capture the authentic, wide-eyed look of innocent wonder on four-year-old Cary Guffey’s face when he opens the door to the glowing alien presence, director Steven Spielberg relied on off-camera practical tricks rather than traditional direction. Knowing he couldn’t simply explain the concept of extraterrestrial awe to a toddler, Spielberg orchestrated a bizarre surprise behind the camera. For different reaction shots during the sequence, he famously deployed a makeup artist dressed in a full gorilla suit wearing a clown mask. When the door opened, the crew member pulled the mask off to elicit a look of genuine shock and confusion from Guffey, and Spielberg also had crew members unwrap presents just out of frame to capture his pure, captivated smile. By manipulating Guffey’s real-time emotions with unexpected visual stimuli, Spielberg successfully grounded the sci-fi spectacle in the unfeigned reality of childhood curiosity.

Close Encounters of the Third Kind (1977), directed by Steven Spielberg, starring Richard Dreyfuss, François Truffaut, Teri Garr, Melinda Dillon, Cary Guffey. After a series of unexplained global anomalies and a personal encounter with a UFO, a blue-collar Indiana utility worker becomes dangerously obsessed with a subliminal vision, driving him to cross the country in search of the truth about humanity’s first contact with alien life.

source_details.synopsis: Close Encounters of the Third Kind is a 1977 American science fiction drama film written and directed by Steven Spielberg, starring Richard Dreyfuss, Melinda Dillon, Teri Garr, Bob Balaban, Cary Guffey, and François Truffaut. The film depicts the interconnected stories of Roy Neary (Dreyfuss), an everyday blue-collar worker in Indiana whose life changes after an encounter with an unidentified flying object (UFO); Jillian Guiler (Dillon), a single mother whose three-year-old son Barry is abducted during the same UFO manifestation; and Claude Lacombe (Truffaut), a French scientist pursuing a link between recent unexplained scientific phenomena across the globe.
